articles.title: The Senate passes the Protect College Sports Act, but the bill's future is unclear

articles.author: Terry Gross
articles.description: MacLachlan was 23 when he auditioned for Lynch's adaptation of Dune. The two would go on to work together on the cult classics Blue Velvet and Twin Peaks. MacLachlan's new memoir is Fictional Selves.
articles.title: Kyle MacLachlan says he was David Lynch's 'submersible' into dark places

articles.author: Maureen Corrigan
articles.description: Min Jin Lee's new novel is the third in a planned four-novel series about the Korean diaspora. Nearly 10 years in the making, this sweeping-but-intimate 600+ page book is overwhelming — in a good way.
articles.title: I didn't think 'Pachinko' could be topped. Then I read 'American Hagwon'

articles.description: New York prosecutors are reopening an investigation into an alleged rape case at Cornell University in 2024. The alleged victim recently filed a lawsuit against seven members of Chi Phi fraternity.
articles.title: Prosecutors are reopening a Cornell fraternity rape case. Here's what we know

articles.author: Kirk Siegler
articles.description: America's farms have largely escaped the president's aggressive immigration crackdown. But as ICE sweeps continue across the nation, farmers are uneasy because many still can't find enough workers.
articles.title: Trump's immigration push has largely spared farms. Idaho dairymen worry it won't last.

articles.title: The Trump administration weakens fuel efficiency standards for new cars

articles.author: Brendan Byrne
articles.description: Starship is key to SpaceX's commercial success and NASA's plans to land humans on the moon. This is the 14th flight of the uncrewed Starship, but the first time it reached orbit.
articles.title: SpaceX's Starship launches on first orbital mission from Texas

articles.author: Rachel Treisman
articles.description: President Trump has brought his New York real estate background to the White House. But experts say D.C. is a very different historic and legal landscape — and worry about the precedent he could set.
articles.title: Trump aims to leave a physical legacy in D.C., bulldozing norms along the way

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Five men arrested on terror charges near a U.S.-run air force base were released on bail, as detectives investigate lines of inquiry, including whether a foreign state or armed group was involved.
articles.title: U.K. examines if Iran or Russia are involved in foiled attack near base used by U.S.

articles.title: 'End Times Fascism' looks at supremacist groups uniting around end-of-the-world ideas

articles.author: Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Widely expected decision is fourth increase to interest rate this year and will be blow to mortgage holders across Australia

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Reserve Bank has lifted its key interest rate to 4.6%, its highest level since 2011, while warning of further hikes.
The widely expected fourth increase to the cash rate this year will add to repayment costs for millions of mortgage holders across the country. Before Tuesday’s meeting, it sat at 4.35%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: RBA interest rates: Reserve Bank hikes cash rate to 4.6%, the highest level since 2011

articles.author: Achol Arok (now), Nick Visser (earlier)
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

New South Wales police say they are investigating the suspicious deaths of two men in the state’s north.
Police said they found the first man – who has since been identified as a 79-year-old – dead at a property on Summerland Way at Gurranang, near Grafton, on 13 September.
And that’s equally important in the Reserve Bank’s mandate, dual mandate, which talks about maintaining full employment at the same time as they go for price stability, which means inflation in the target band.
Well, it’s still lower than what we saw under Howard and Costello, is the first point.
I think that’s pretty clear. And what we’ve seen in recent years is that it’s possible to have low and steady unemployment at the same time as we see inflation moderate to more normal levels.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: RBA hikes official cash rate to highest level since 2011 as Chalmers says move ‘will make things tougher’ for many Australians

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Analysts believe PM has a ‘golden opportunity’ to offer older people better protection in return for weakening the triple lock guarantee
It is a brave party leader who is prepared to go into an election promising a multibillion-pound new public service – likely to be funded by tax rises or holding back increases in the state pension.
But Andy Burnham’s colleagues are excited about the confident promise of new social care system that seven previous prime ministers have failed to deliver.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We have time to make our case’: Labour insiders are confident Burnham can sell his social care reforms

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
New leader expected to be chosen imminently, with Mehreen Faruqi, David Shoebridge and Hanson-Young among frontrunners

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

High-profile Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young has confirmed she will run for the party’s leadership, promising to bring the fight to Labor and One Nation after Larissa Waters’ shock resignation.
The party’s longest-serving federal MP, Hanson-Young confirmed on social media she was discussing a tilt at the leadership with colleagues on Tuesday, ahead of a two-day party retreat in Sydney, when the new leader will be chosen.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sarah Hanson-Young announces Greens leadership tilt after MPs blindsided by Larissa Waters’ shock resignation

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
The UK communities secretary decried protests by ‘men in black wearing face masks’ and those ‘whipping up hatred’ towards lifeboat volunteers
Far-right marches led by the self-styled “Danny Tommo” should not be treated like normal protests, the communities secretary, Angela Rayner, has said, calling the marches “intimidation” that should not be permitted.
Rayner said the behaviour of some masked marchers – who have blocked roads and transport hubs – was not an acceptable form of protest.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Intimidatory’ far-right marches should not be allowed, says Angela Rayner

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
The US secretary of state offered no evidence for his claims, and also said many people were ‘disturbed’ that the five suspects had been released on bail
US secretary of state Marco Rubio has said unequivocally that a foreign actor was involved in the suspected UK bomb plot at RAF Fairford, hours after the five suspects arrested close to the airbase were released on bail.
“What could have happened in the UK over the weekend is a ‌very serious situation,” Rubio said in an interview with Fox News on Monday evening, adding that it “clearly involves the hands ‌of a foreign actor.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rubio says foreign actor was ‘clearly’ behind suspected RAF Fairford bomb plot

articles.author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
articles.description:
Chief strategy officer to fly to Australia to front joint committee on AI after breaches of government websites

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

OpenAI has apologised to Australians for its agent attack on Medicare, and will front parliament next week, as the tech company revealed more details about its June hack of Australian government websites.
In a blog post released on Tuesday, OpenAI said it should have handled its response better.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘New kind of cyber incident’: OpenAI apologises for Medicare hack and reveals extent of attack

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell (now); Shrai Popat and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

While the lawmakers in the US House have already left Washington to get a head start on midterm campaigning, the Senate is hoping to wrap up its legislative agenda this week. Today, we can expect a vote at 5.30pm ET on the Protect College Sports act, which attempts to provide greater protections for university athletes in the US.
The bill includes provisions for players to earn compensation from their name, image and likeness – known as NIL payments, and allow them to transfer schools (and teams) without being penalized or forced to sit out for a defined period of time. If the legislation clears the Senate it will still need to head back to the lower chamber before it can head to Donald Trump’s desk for his signature.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump doubles down on claims US will win war with Iran ‘one way or another’ as talks are in doubt – as it happened

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Former Sydney police officer, 31, has pleaded not guilty to murdering AFL umpire Jesse Baird and flight attendant Luke Davies

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Brand new AFL shorts, a Qantas card and other bloodied belongings were found in a dumpster two days after football umpire Jesse Baird and flight attendant Luke Davies were allegedly murdered, a Sydney court has heard.
Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting the couple with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Looked like dried blood’: worker tells Beau Lamarre-Condon trial about finding suspicious belongings in skip

articles.author: Australian Associated Press and Tory Shepherd
articles.description:
Detained anti-human trafficking campaigners include Tran Hiep, a Vietnamese Australian, not heard from since 18 September 
Vietnamese authorities have detained three activists, including a Norwegian and an Australian, on what have been described as “fabricated” charges.
The Vietnamese government said the three confessed to being members of Viet Tan – a pro-democracy organisation – which it describes as a terrorist group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Vietnamese government accused of abducting human rights activists

articles.author: Abené Clayton and agencies
articles.description:
Lawyers for Christa Pike, 50, convicted of killing classmate in Knoxville in 1995, ask supreme court to grant stay
Christa Pike, a woman who was convicted of murder 30 years ago, is set to be put to death on Wednesday after her request for clemency was denied by Tennessee governor Bill Lee on Monday. If the execution goes through, she will be the first woman executed in the state in 200 years.
Pike, who is now 50, was 18 when she and her boyfriend, who was 17 at the time, killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, one of their classmate at Knoxville Job Corps in 1995.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tennessee to execute a woman for first time in 200 years after governor denies clemency

articles.author: Abené Clayton
articles.description:
Police arrest couple in their 70s after Jonathan McKinsey, 40, found dead in park in Bay Area city of Dublin
A married couple in their 70s have been arrested for allegedly shooting and killing their son-in-law, a New York Times engineer, in broad daylight at a suburban Bay Area park.
A police officer found Jonathan McKinsey, 40, lying on the ground with multiple gunshot wounds in a park in Dublin, California, a small city about 35 miles (56.3km) east of San Francisco. Around the time the officer discovered him, 911 calls began pouring in from witnesses reporting the shooting.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: In-laws arrested on suspicion of murder after New York Times engineer shot dead in California

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
GPT-6.1 Astra showed deceptive behavior and tried to use external tools despite knowing it would be unsafe
OpenAI is scrapping the release of GPT-6.1 Astra, a next-generation ⁠AI model planned for an October debut, over safety concerns raised by researchers ⁠during internal testing, the ⁠Wall ​Street Journal reported on Monday.
The model, expected to appear in ChatGPT and ⁠Codex, was designed to handle more complex tasks without human assistance, the report said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: OpenAI scraps release of new model over safety concerns in internal testing

articles.author: Richard Luscombe and Maya Yang
articles.description:
Outrage over treatment of alleged offenders, members of Chi Phi fraternity, has grown since lawsuit was made public

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

Prosecutors in New York said on Monday that they have reopened an investigation into the alleged gang-rape of a student at Cornell University after an outcry over “leniency” shown to seven fraternity members named as the perpetrators.
According to lawyers for the student, who filed a civil lawsuit against the university and her alleged attackers earlier in September, only two members of the Chi Phi fraternity were expelled after the October 2024 incident, in which she said she was drugged and repeatedly raped over the course of seven hours.
Information and support for anyone affected by rape or sexual abuse issues is available from the following organizations. In the US, Rainn offers support on 800-656-4673. In the UK, Rape Crisis offers support on 0808 500 2222. In Australia, support is available at 1800Respect (1800 737 732). Other international helplines can be found at ibiblio.org/rcip/internl.html
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Investigation of alleged gang-rape at Cornell University fraternity house reopened

articles.author: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent
articles.description:
Police say alleged offences could have been committed ‘knowingly or unknowingly’ on behalf of a foreign state
Five men arrested over a suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford have been released on bail as police investigate why they were so close to the airbase in three vans with suspicious material in the back.
The five suspects were revealed to be British men, all in their 20s and from London. They had been arrested in the Gloucestershire countryside early on Sunday morning on suspicion of explosives offences and preparing an act of terrorism, with an Iranian link a key line of inquiry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Five UK nationals arrested near RAF Fairford released on bail

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Tehran has been trying to step up attacks on targets in the west but its track record has been mixed
Investigators may be some way from determining exactly what led five men with three vans to a village just outside RAF Fairford in the small hours of Sunday – but the fact they have all been released on bail without immediate charge suggests they are not deemed to pose a serious and violent threat.
In a moment where wider geopolitical tensions mean external threats are perceived to be close, the question of whether Iran had a hand in the alleged plot remains open. Nonetheless, the bailing of the men is a mercifully lower-key development in an investigation that appeared of the utmost gravity.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Questions remain over Iran’s link to alleged RAF Fairford bomb plot

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Amid conflicting statements, local MP and councillors demand answers over how suspects were allowed to enter residential areas of nearby village
An MP and councillors representing the residents of the village near RAF Fairford who were evacuated due to a suspected terror plot have expressed scepticism and concern over the security response to threats made by Iran.
About 85 properties in Whelford, Gloucestershire, were evacuated on Sunday morning after five men were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences in the village. The men, who were later re-arrested on suspicion of terror offences, were released on bail on Monday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Local representatives question official accounts after suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
National Rally and allies gain record 14 seats and can form senate group for first time after indirect vote by local officials
The French far-right leader Marine Le Pen has said her 2027 presidential campaign will be boosted after her anti-immigration party, the National Rally (RN), and its allies improved to a record 14 seats in partial senate elections this weekend.
Le Pen called the results a “historic victory” and a “major milestone” after her party cleared the 10-seat threshold to be able to form a senate group for the first time, after an indirect vote by local officials including mayors and councillors.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Marine Le Pen hails RN senate surge as ‘milestone’ towards French presidency

articles.author: Kim Willsher in Paris
articles.description:
Campaign broadcast across France encourages people to come forward even if they have little to no memory of attack
Gisèle Pelicot is the figurehead of a new campaign run by her daughter to encourage people who suspect they have been drugged and sexually assaulted to come forward, even if they have little to no memory of the attack.
Caroline Darian, 47, who believes she was also drugged and assaulted by her father, Dominique Pelicot – her mother’s ex-husband – launched a primetime public information push on Monday across France’s television network, on social media, in the press and on posters.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gisèle Pelicot’s daughter launches awareness campaign for potential victims of drugging and sexual assault

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Marie-Celestin Karondwa was attacked on Sunday after promoting measures to prevent spread of disease, his party says

A senior member of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ruling party was beaten to death on Sunday after appearing on a radio programme to raise awareness about the Ebola outbreak, a party representative has said.
Marie-Celestin Karondwa, the acting president of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party’s federal executive committee in Butembo, a new hotspot for the outbreak, was attacked after taking part in a ​radio show during which he ‌promoted prevention measures for the disease, ‌the UDPS federation in the city said in a statement, Reuters reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: DRC politician beaten to death after radio appearance about Ebola outbreak

articles.author: Pjotr Sauer in Kyiv
articles.description:
Three others wounded as jet-powered drones increasingly target Ukraine’s capital, with medical centre also hit

A Russian drone hit the National Academy of Sciences in central Kyiv on Monday, killing at least one person, in the latest daytime attack on Ukraine’s capital.
Flames tore through the historic building as people clambered out of first- and second-floor windows to escape, in dramatic scenes increasingly familiar in the heavily bombarded city.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Daytime Russian strike on Kyiv’s science academy kills at least one

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
EU to push member states to cut tax rate below duty on gas, with 11% surge in sales also put down to fallout from Iran war

Business live – latest updates

Europe live – latest updates

Sales of residential heat pumps increased 11% across Europe in the first six months of the year as the Iran war sent oil and gas prices rocketing and some countries lowered electricity taxes.
Homeowners bought 1.16m heat pumps across 12 European countries, up from 1.05m in the first half of 2025, according to the European Heat Pump Association (EHPA).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Heat pump sales soar across Europe after states cut electricity taxes, data shows

articles.author: Rajeev Syal and agencies
articles.description:
Official says deaths – and dozens of injuries – were probably caused by crushing on boat carrying 105 people
A 10-year-old child and two women died ⁠attempting ​to cross the Channel on Monday, French authorities have said.
Their deaths and the injuries of dozens of others in a large dinghy were probably caused by crushing, according to a French official.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Three people dead, including a child, in attempt to cross Channel to UK

articles.author: Patrick Wintour and Emma Graham-Harrison
articles.description:
Former attorney general Dominic Grieve says Israel is not entitled to shut mission in occupied Palestinian territory

UK politics live – latest updates

Israel does not have a legal right to act on its plan to close the British consulate in East Jerusalem, the former attorney general Dominic Grieve has advised the UK Foreign Office.
Israel has said it intends to shut the consulate on 8 October in response to the sweeping ban on trade with goods from Israeli settlements announced by the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, this month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israel does not have right to close UK consulate in Jerusalem, Foreign Office advised

articles.author: Amy Hawkins and agencies
articles.description:
David Perdue’s remarks come after a Taiwanese minister spoke of the ‘severe’ military threat posed by Beijing to the self-ruled island
Donald Trump offered to sell weapons to China while hosting its leader, Xi Jinping, last week, the US ambassador to China said on Sunday.
David Perdue told Fox News on Sunday: “President Trump continues to say, hey, we sell arms to other people around the world. He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump asked Xi Jinping if China would like to buy US weapons, American ambassador says

articles.author: James Parrish for MetDesk
articles.description:
Capital city submerged in waist-high flood water, while elsewhere Hurricane Nolo threatens Hawaii’s Big Island
Bangkok was declared a disaster zone by its city officials towards the end of last week, after streets in Thailand’s capital city were submerged in up to waist-high flood water. The flooding stemmed from an active cell of low pressure across central Thailand that brought continuous heavy rainfall and thunderstorms to Bangkok and surrounding regions.
The heavy rain began early on Thursday when the weak area of low pressure travelled north-westwards up the gulf of Thailand before then sitting over central Thailand by Friday morning. For most of the following two days this low pressure remained roughly in situ, which allowed unrelenting downpours over Bangkok and nearby areas. One weather station near Prachin Buri, just north-east of the capital, recorded 213.5mm within a 24-hour period between Friday and Saturday evening local time – for comparison, London receives an average 585mm a year). Fortunately, the centre of the low-pressure cell shifted north-westwards on Sunday and brought an end to the torrential rainfall.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bangkok declared a ‘disaster zone’ after flooding, as rainstorms shift direction

articles.author: Nasser al-Sakkaf in Taiz and William Christou
articles.description:
Renewed fighting between Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces has shattered four years of relative calm
In the mornings, 13-year-old Muneer Farie went to school, and in the afternoons he helped his father feed the livestock. He took his studies seriously, dreaming of becoming the first teacher in his family of farmers.
As fighting approached his village in al-Wazeyah district in Taiz, Yemen, two weeks ago, Muneer’s focus started to drift from his lessons. The classroom echoed with the distant sounds of explosions and gunfire. His home was suddenly on the frontline of renewed fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Children forced to give up school for work as fighting upends daily life in Yemen

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Foreign secretary will tell party’s conference ‘we are not here to accept the status quo but to change it’
Ed Miliband will tell campaigners and party members who raised the plight of Palestinians they were right that Labour’s approach had not been enough, saying he was heeding the calls of millions of people by imposing sanctions on Israeli settlements.
The foreign secretary will tell the Labour party conference that the government will take more explicitly progressive foreign policy positions under Andy Burnham, and that the UK will be a leader among like-minded countries in a new age of diplomacy.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘You were right’: Ed Miliband tells critics Labour was wrong on Gaza

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Slinger Francisco, who performed as the Mighty Sparrow, died on Sunday surrounded by family in New York
Slinger Francisco, known on stage as the Mighty Sparrow and dubbed the “calypso king of the world”, has died aged 91.
Francisco, who got his breakthrough in calypso music with his 1956 hit song Jean and Dinah, died peacefully surrounded by his family in New York on Sunday, his family said in a statement.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mighty Sparrow, the Trinidad and Tobago singer known as the ‘calypso king of the world’, dies aged 91

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Hurricane Nolo is moving away from Hawaiian islands but threat of heavy rain, flash floods and strong winds persists
Hurricane Nolo was moving away from the Hawaiian islands on Sunday, but the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding and strong winds persisted in areas of the island chain still recovering from previous storms.
Nolo was about 365 miles (585km) south-south-west of Honolulu and moving away from the Big Island at about 12mph (19km/h). But the Hawaii county civil defense agency said a high wind warning, wind advisory and high surf advisory remained in effect for parts of the island through Sunday evening as Nolo’s maximum sustained winds rose to 115mph.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hurricane Nolo still threatens Hawaii as Mexico’s Baja braces for Hurricane Polo

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Waltz says Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to end war because they ‘were asking for everything up front’
The Trump administration’s ambassador to the United Nations said the US rejected Iran’s proposal to end the ongoing war there because Iranian negotiators “were asking for everything up front”.
Echoing comments by Donald Trump on Saturday, the president’s UN ambassador, Mike Waltz, told CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday that Iran had asked for relief “from billions and billions of sanctions that are going into place” as part of an economic blockade on Iran. The blockade is aimed at putting pressure on Iran to stop its attacks ‌on vessels in the strait of Hormuz.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UN ambassador Waltz says Iran was not negotiating ‘in good faith’ to end war

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg and agencies
articles.description:
Seventeen people killed near Johannesburg in suspected ‘illegal goldmining turf war’, as 10 killed in separate incident at barbecue venue near Cape Town
Two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, as the country grapples with one of the world’s highest murder rates amid investigations into corruption and criminality within the police.
The South African police service said on Sunday that 17 people were killed on Saturday night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 assault rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, about 50 miles south-west of central Johannesburg. At least 15 other people sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least 27 dead after two mass shootings in South Africa, police say

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Ping Ping and Fu Shuang to live at Atlanta zoo in Georgia as part of loan deal between Chinese and US governments
Two giant pandas from China arrived in Atlanta, Georgia, on Sunday morning as part of an agreement between the Chinese and US governments.
While in Washington DC for a three-day summit with Donald Trump, the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, announced that the pandas would arrive in Atlanta in the coming days. The loan of the pandas to the Atlanta zoo was one of the few concrete outcomes of Xi’s state visit with the US president, which saw expressions of goodwill between the leaders, but no fixes to any of the longstanding differences between the two countries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two giant pandas arrive in Atlanta from China after Xi-Trump summit

articles.author: Gloria Dickie
articles.description:
Two troops of chacma baboons are breaking into homes and shops but animal rights activists insist coexistence is the answer
Cape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents. The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered.
Cape Town’s baboon problem has been brewing since the 2000s, after the city stopped culling troops in the late 1990s after pressure from the public. But in the past two years it has reached boiling point. A 2025 census found that the population had grown by a third since 2000, from 360 baboons to 493, now living in 12 managed troops.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Loved ones describe Jordan Yap, 30, as an experienced hiker who set out for a 10-day solo trek Peru before falling silent

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Loved ones of a missing Australian trekker who was last seen nearly two weeks ago on a remote South American hiking trail are urging local authorities to help with the search.
A wide-scale sweep by a private rescue crew has so far failed to find any trace of 30-year-old Jordan Yap, who last made contact with friends and family on 14 September ahead of a planned 10-day solo trek along Peru’s Huayhuash mountain range, 400km north-east of Lima.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Melbourne man’s mysterious disappearance on popular Peru hiking trail prompts widespread search

articles.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
articles.description:
Attorney says fishers ‘losing their livelihoods’, but Marco Rubio maintains US still willing to ‘blow up ships if need be’
While the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, was being decorated in Quito by Ecuador’s president for “helping to promote peace in the region”, 10 Ecuadorian fishers whose boat had been blown up by US forces were adrift in the eastern Pacific.
On 8 September, a day before Rubio arrived, a US patrol vessel intercepted the fishing boat Don Rufo in international waters near Ecuador.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US strikes on Ecuadorian fishing boats raise humanitarian concerns but Trump admin not wavering

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
President’s ‘hard, drastic and necessary measure’, likely to attract widespread public support, polls suggest
The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has signed an order banning fixed-odds sports betting just over a week before the first round of the presidential election, in a move he said was designed to tackle the pervasive problem of families falling into debt.
The decision ends the operation, offering, intermediation and advertising of betting.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lula bans fixed-odds sports betting a week before Brazilian elections

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad and Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Tens of thousands of police deployed and roads barricaded as PTI party demands release of jailed former PM
Leaders from Imran Khan’s party have vowed to go ahead with a nationwide demonstration in Pakistan to demand the former prime minister’s release, even as the government deployed tens of thousands of police to Islamabad, barricaded highways and issued arrest warrants to try to stop the march.
The state has taken extreme measures to prevent Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party from proceeding with the march. It was announced after mounting concerns of the treatment of Khan, who has been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan locks down Islamabad as Imran Khan’s party vows to march on capital

articles.author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
articles.description:
While US president hailed visit as ‘great’, almost nothing of substance was achieved on resolving thorny issues

Key takeaways from the Trump-Xi summit in Washington

If the Beijing meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in May was the “stalemate summit”, the second round of talks between the presidents of the US and China this week seemed to give up entirely on the idea of breakthroughs.
Instead, it was described as a celebration of “diplotainment” rather than diplomacy, where pomp prevailed over progress and where one of the main outcomes was the news that two giant pandas would soon be sent from China to Atlanta zoo.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pomp over progress in Xi’s US summit with Trump is a win for China

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Fighting escalates after Tigrayan rebels form new coalition aimed at overthrowing Abiy Ahmed government
There are growing fears of a return to civil war in Ethiopia after an offensive by fighters from Tigray into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of the prime minister, Abiy Ahmed.
About 600,000 people died between 2020 and 2022 during a devastating war between the Ethiopian army and the political party and paramilitary group the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides are now accusing the other of triggering a return to open conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rebel offensive against Ethiopian army stokes fears of return to civil war

articles.author: Rachel Hall and Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
Role for Anant Ambani, son of India’s richest person, who also runs a controversial mega-zoo, met with incredulity
Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability.
The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Backlash as Indian oil heir made professor of sustainability by Newcastle University

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Sunil Bharti Mittal’s Airtel Money targets $9bn IPO in boost for ailing UK stock market
Nils Pratley: Does this mark the end of London’s listing drought? Not yet
A payments business that operates across Africa and is ultimately controlled by an Indian billionaire has announced its intention to float on the struggling London Stock Exchange.
Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of Airtel Africa, is planning one of the biggest UK listings in years, in a boost for the shrinking London market that has faced a string of recent departures.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Islamic State-inspired bombings of churches and hotels in 2019 was one of the country’s worst ever attacks
A court in Sri Lanka has convicted 15 men on terrorist charges for their involvement in the deadly 2019 Easter bombings and sentenced them each to at least 220 years in prison.
The terror attacks, which targeted luxury hotels and churches as they held Easter services, left 267 people dead and wounded almost 600. The bombings, which were inspired by Islamic State (IS), were among the deadliest terror attacks in Sri Lanka’s history and sent shockwaves through the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings: 15 sentenced to hundreds of years in prison each over deadly terror attacks

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
Generations of artisans from Mumbai to Lucknow have shaped the world’s most coveted designs. Plus, the gen Z memes giving classic Bollywood a new life
The zardozi embroidery on a Dior dress, the T-strap leather sandals at a Prada show, the mirror-work technique used on a Fendi bag – for decades, the skill of Indian artisans has been an invisible force behind some of the world’s most coveted fashion.
Now, that work is beginning to claim its own place in the spotlight, and the Mumbai-based textile and embroidery atelier Chanakya International is at the forefront.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘What we have is unique’: the Indian craftsmanship behind global luxury fashion

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad and Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Police crack down on family and political supporters of former PM who say authorities are ‘slowly killing’ him in prison
Three sisters of Pakistan’s incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan have been arrested amid a heavy-handed government crackdown on plans for a nationwide protest to demand Khan’s release.
The lawyer for the three sisters, Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, said on Monday that they had all been detained and jailed for 30 days under a warrant that accused them of being a threat to public order.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan jails sisters of Imran Khan before protest seeking his release

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Decision from conservative justice comes before court hears case on whether fossil-fuel firms deceived US public
Supreme court justice Samuel Alito recused himself on Monday from a major climate-change case after facing calls to step aside due to stock holdings in oil companies.
A letter posted in the case did not specify a reason, but the conservative justice has previously recused himself from other cases involving companies where he holds stock.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Samuel Alito steps aside in a major climate case amid scrutiny over oil stock holdings

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
President says plant will be built by Indian-owned company and calls it largest such facility in American history
Donald Trump on Monday announced what he called the largest steel plant in American history to be built in Iowa, giving Republicans a jobs message to take to voters in a state that could help decide control of the Senate in November.
“Using advanced steelmaking technology, the plant will produce some of the highest quality, most affordable steel anywhere in the world,” Trump said in the Oval Office, flanked by Iowa’s top Republicans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump announces $15bn Iowa steel plant as he bids to boost flagging midterm hopes

articles.author: Ariana Baio
articles.description:
Andrew Bailey will resign as FBI co-deputy director about a year after assuming the position
Andrew Bailey, a deputy director of the FBI who has been overseeing some of Trump’s election-related investigations, will step down from his position approximately one year after assuming his role.
“I am announcing that I am stepping down to return to my family in Missouri,” Bailey wrote in an X post on Monday amid an ongoing shake-up at the bureau.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump appointee overseeing election investigations steps down from FBI role

articles.author: Ashifa Kassam European community affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Sending migrants to countries they do not come from can have deadly consequences and must be halted, says report
The deportation of thousands of migrants from the US to third countries has set off a “cascade of human rights violations” that could have “deadly” consequences, two dozen UN human rights experts have warned.
Since Donald Trump returned to power in 2025, the US government has been offering millions of dollars to foreign governments to take in migrants, including refugees and asylum seekers, with no ties to their countries. Deals have been struck with 35 nations, nearly a third of them in Africa.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s deportations to third countries violate human rights, UN experts warn

articles.author: Ariana Baio
articles.description:
Bo French, who is running to lead a state agency, has in the past posted controversial and racist statements online
Bo French, a Texas Republican running to lead a powerful state agency, has a history of making controversial social media posts, including calling for the public execution of Democratic leaders, according to a recent investigation from CNN’s KFile team.
French, who is running to lead Texas’s railroad commission, has recently faced criticism from members of his own party after making a racist post on social media. Powerful Republicans, including the Texas senator John Cornyn, said they would not support French in the upcoming election.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Texas Republican called for public execution of Democratic leaders – report

articles.author: Moira Donegan
articles.description:
The US has already grown used to the horror caused by abortion bans. And Republicans have sought to quash the stories
Abortion has faded from the headlines since the Dobbs decision of 2022, and Republicans like it that way. In the immediate aftermath of the supreme court’s overturning of Roe v Wade, as millions of women lost access to the dignity and self-determination that abortion provided them, clinics shut their doors, and the extent of Dobbs’s horrendously adverse public health implications started to become clear, abortion was always, it seemed, in the headlines. There were plenty of stories. There was the first known woman to die as the result of an abortion ban; and then the second; and then the third. There were the various lawsuits and ballot initiatives that for a while turned a…
articles.title: Why has abortion faded from America’s national conversation? | Moira Donegan

articles.author: Maanvi Singh, Will Craft, Andrew Witherspoon and Julius Constantine Motal
articles.description:
After public backlash, the Trump administration changed its tactics from ‘siege’ to ‘soft feet’. Now, ICE is everywhere
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gone in 90 seconds: an ‘invisibilized’ ICE is arresting more people than ever

articles.author: Zach Vasquez
articles.description:
There are some promising moments from newer cast members, but the show’s return, after a politically tumultuous period, was lacking in bite
The 52nd season of Saturday Night Live opens inside the New York City mayor’s office. Mayor Zohran Mamdani (Ramy Youssef, reprising the role from last season) gets a surprise visit from Donald Trump (James Austin Johnson). The president, who “for some reason that no one can figure out” loves Mamdani, has braved the big El Niño storm to visit his “day one”.
Trump unloads about his busy week – banning members of the press from the White House pool, delivering apocalyptic threats to Iran at the UN, consulting with AI leaders including Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg (“It made me think, wow, RFK Jr’s probably right about those vaccines, I mean, the ‘tizz in that room …”) – before being interrupted by his assistant Natalie Harp (Ashley Padilla). Acting like “the girl from Obsession, but blond”, the dangerously jealous Harp threatens Mamdani. Trump eventually convinces the mayor to let him stay and hang out in New York in exchange for $20bn for a housing project in Queens.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saturday Night Live: Jalen Brunson makes for stiff host in underwhelming season premiere

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
President has let rip with swearwords in recent months, redefining norms about acceptable language in public office
With a lifetime of political memories stretching back to John F Kennedy’s assassination and the Black civil rights struggles of the 1960s, Cheryl Johnson had one complaint above all else about today’s politicians: the swearing.
“All this cursing in politics, we never heard that before,” said Johnson, a retired social worker living in the Pittsburgh area. “Words are very powerful, and the past 45 presidents of this country, have not used such vile language.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bad language: profane Trump brings presidential swearing out into open

articles.author: Dave Schilling
articles.description:
The streaming channel was full of the president’s vanity and myopia. It was also deeply, deeply dull
Are you currently at an airport? Strapped to a hospital bed, with various tubes protruding from your body? Maybe you’re on a treadmill or visiting an elder care facility? Chained to a radiator in the basement from the Saw movies?
If you said yes to any of these questions, you might be watching cable news while reading this column. Or maybe you’re one of the hundreds of people currently watching Donald Trump’s answer to cable news, Trump TV – a YouTube streaming channel that airs nothing but White House-sanctioned content 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
Dave Schilling is a Los Angeles-based writer and humorist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: I spent a full hour watching Trump TV. It’s a digital pathway to hell | Dave Schilling

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
As she mulls another presidential run, the former VP is building bridges with progressive and Arab American leaders
Does Donald Trump secretly want Republicans to get annihilated in the midterms? Because he’s certainly acting that way. He continues to brush off concerns about the cost of living, saying last week that high gas prices are a very “inexpensive price to pay” for the war on Iran.
And, of course, the president seems to have no plans to end that disastrous war, apart from making vague threats about blowing the entire country up. Trust me, he keeps saying, everything will get better after the midterms. But by the looks of his dismal polling numbers, not many people are swallowing his empty promises anymore.
Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kamala Harris is belatedly courting progressives. Is it too little, too late? | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Richard Luscombe
articles.description:
Third US president wrote in 1787 about importance of peace, paying off debt and supporting agriculture
A remarkably prescient letter written by Thomas Jefferson, the third US president, advising how the newly created country could prosper, has been put up for sale by a private collector. The handwritten document from 1787 warns specifically against many of the missteps Donald Trump has taken to drag down his own second term of office.
Written in Paris, where Jefferson was the fledgling government’s minister to France, the note to David Rittenhouse, a friend and fellow member of the American Philosophical Society, muses on the priorities and principles he believed future presidents should follow.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thomas Jefferson letter goes on the market – containing a prescient warning for Trump today

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
The Chinese leader’s visit to Washington appears to have done nothing to shift the stalemate in bilateral relations 
Within days, two high-profile Chinese visitors will arrive in the US – envoys of friendship, as Xi Jinping described them when he met Donald Trump at the White House this week. The giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will be hosted at Atlanta zoo. Beijing dispatched the first panda pair to the US in 1972 following President Richard Nixon’s landmark visit to China. It uses the animals to indicate satisfaction or displeasure with other nations. But it also charges heftily for their lease: reportedly, around $1m a year per pair. Americans’ views of China have warmed from a pandemic nadir, but are unlikely to be shifted much by two animals, however charming. These days they are more of a token gesture than a striking symbol.
It is telling that the announcement was one of the main takeaways of Mr Xi’s visit to Washington. Expectations were low after May’s stalemate summit in Beijing, but this meeting still struggled to meet them. The US president gave Mr Xi a lavish welcome – unusually, travelling to meet the “strong, vibrant and fit” Chinese leader off the plane. He insisted that they had “never gotten along better”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on Trump and Xi: a show of friendship, but no real attempt to address the tensions | Editorial

articles.author: Marina Hyde, Nosheen Iqbal, Laurence Topham, Ruth Abrahams, Ben Kape and Sami Kent
articles.description:
The Guardian’s award-winning columnist talks to Nosheen Iqbal about Donald Trump's ballroom, going for a drink with Nigel Farage, Taylor Swift’s wedding, and why she's feeling relaxed about the AI apocalypse
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Marina Hyde on Trump's home improvements, tech bros and Taylor Swift – video

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland , with Shrai Popat , produced by Danielle Stephens and Nada Smiljanic
articles.description:
The US press corps stood up to Donald Trump this week after he banned three organisations he doesn’t like from the White House. But when it came to the leader of one of the US’s oldest adversaries – China – well, Trump literally rolled out a very long red carpet. Jonathan Freedland speaks to the Guardian’s Shrai Popat about why Trump seems weaker these days, but why it could be dangerous to underestimate him
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump picked a fight with the media... and lost | Politics Weekly America

articles.description:
CNN senior reporter Betsy Klein gained access to the White House on 24 September, hours after a federal judge ruled against Donald Trump's media ban. The ban had barred reporters from CNN, MS Now and Politico from accessing the White House
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CNN reporter arrives at White House after judge rules against Trump's media ban – video

articles.description:
Protesters in Austin, Texas, demonstrated against the Trump administration’s hardline anti-immigration campaign after an ICE agent shot and wounded a man on Sunday afternoon. Eyewitness footage filmed moments after the shooting shows the ICE officer standing next to an open car door, in which there is a visible dent. The man, identified by relatives and his lawyer as 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, was taken to a hospital in Austin in a serious but stable condition, officials said, before being taken into custody.
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, said it was leading an investigation into the officer involved in the shooting, with the help of the FBI. Austin police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting, which occurred after a traffic stop, mayor Kirk Watson stated at a press conference 

ICE agent shoots and wounds Venezuelan man at traffic stop in Austin, Texas

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Protesters gather in Austin after ICE agent shoots and wounds man – video

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Analysts believe PM has a ‘golden opportunity’ to offer older people better protection in return for weakening the triple lock guarantee
It is a brave party leader who is prepared to go into an election promising a multibillion-pound new public service – likely to be funded by tax rises or holding back increases in the state pension.
But Andy Burnham’s colleagues are excited about the confident promise of new social care system that seven previous prime ministers have failed to deliver.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We have time to make our case’: Labour insiders are confident Burnham can sell his social care reforms

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
The UK communities secretary decried protests by ‘men in black wearing face masks’ and those ‘whipping up hatred’ towards lifeboat volunteers
Far-right marches led by the self-styled “Danny Tommo” should not be treated like normal protests, the communities secretary, Angela Rayner, has said, calling the marches “intimidation” that should not be permitted.
Rayner said the behaviour of some masked marchers – who have blocked roads and transport hubs – was not an acceptable form of protest.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Intimidatory’ far-right marches should not be allowed, says Angela Rayner

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
The US secretary of state offered no evidence for his claims, and also said many people were ‘disturbed’ that the five suspects had been released on bail
US secretary of state Marco Rubio has said unequivocally that a foreign actor was involved in the suspected UK bomb plot at RAF Fairford, hours after the five suspects arrested close to the airbase were released on bail.
“What could have happened in the UK over the weekend is a ‌very serious situation,” Rubio said in an interview with Fox News on Monday evening, adding that it “clearly involves the hands ‌of a foreign actor.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rubio says foreign actor was ‘clearly’ behind suspected RAF Fairford bomb plot

articles.author: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent
articles.description:
Police say alleged offences could have been committed ‘knowingly or unknowingly’ on behalf of a foreign state
Five men arrested over a suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford have been released on bail as police investigate why they were so close to the airbase in three vans with suspicious material in the back.
The five suspects were revealed to be British men, all in their 20s and from London. They had been arrested in the Gloucestershire countryside early on Sunday morning on suspicion of explosives offences and preparing an act of terrorism, with an Iranian link a key line of inquiry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Five UK nationals arrested near RAF Fairford released on bail

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Tehran has been trying to step up attacks on targets in the west but its track record has been mixed
Investigators may be some way from determining exactly what led five men with three vans to a village just outside RAF Fairford in the small hours of Sunday – but the fact they have all been released on bail without immediate charge suggests they are not deemed to pose a serious and violent threat.
In a moment where wider geopolitical tensions mean external threats are perceived to be close, the question of whether Iran had a hand in the alleged plot remains open. Nonetheless, the bailing of the men is a mercifully lower-key development in an investigation that appeared of the utmost gravity.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Questions remain over Iran’s link to alleged RAF Fairford bomb plot

articles.author: Kiran Stacey, Jessica Elgot and Pippa Crerar
articles.description:
Exclusive: Creation of GB Grid will be major step towards putting Britain’s utility companies into public control 
Andy Burnham will take his first major step to putting Britain’s utility companies into public control when, at the Labour conference, he announces a new government-backed body to invest in the electricity grid.
The prime minister will use his first speech as party leader to announce the creation of GB Grid, which will use money previously allocated to Great British Energy to compete with privately owned companies such as National Grid.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham promises to roll back privatisation with government-backed grid plan

articles.author: Kiran Stacey and Pippa Crerar
articles.description:
Miatta Fahnbulleh says Britain must look at how costs are recovered – and that could mean money off bills
Billions of pounds worth of green levies could be taken off bills, the energy secretary has said, as the government investigates funding green infrastructure through taxes instead.
Miatta Fahnbulleh is looking at how green projects are funded, including varying levies between customers and funding them all through general taxation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cost of green transition could be spread among UK taxpayers, energy secretary suggests

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Amid conflicting statements, local MP and councillors demand answers over how suspects were allowed to enter residential areas of nearby village
An MP and councillors representing the residents of the village near RAF Fairford who were evacuated due to a suspected terror plot have expressed scepticism and concern over the security response to threats made by Iran.
About 85 properties in Whelford, Gloucestershire, were evacuated on Sunday morning after five men were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences in the village. The men, who were later re-arrested on suspicion of terror offences, were released on bail on Monday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Local representatives question official accounts after suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford

articles.author: Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
Former journalist and honorary life president of Norwich City FC died peacefully at home on Monday
Michael Wynn-Jones, the journalist and husband of the TV chef Delia Smith, has died at the age of 85.
Wynn-Jones was honorary life president of Norwich City football club, which said everyone at the club was “deeply saddened” by his death.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Michael Wynn-Jones, husband of Delia Smith, dies aged 85

articles.author: Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey with Miatta Fahnbulleh, produced by Nada Smiljanic and Zoe Hitch; music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
Speaking to Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey at the Labour party conference in Liverpool, Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, said a mark of her success or failure would be whether she could get bills down and said she would do so. She also challenged Reform UK and the Tories on their climate inaction, saying they would eventually ‘bow’ because they were on the ‘wrong side of history’
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘They will bow’: energy secretary challenges Reform and Tories – podcast

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
Row comes amid rising division and a tendency towards cynical political posturing in Northern Ireland
Three decades ago, it took the deaths of three Roman Catholic children – the Quinn brothers, Jason, nine, Mark, 10, and 11-year-old Richard – in a petrol bomb attack to bring an end to the Drumcree dispute. “No road is worth a life, let alone the lives of three little boys,” the Orange Order’s County Armagh chaplain said at the time.
It is perhaps extraordinary to think that this could ever have needed saying – but that was then. Northern Ireland is very different place today.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Absence of violence in Drumcree does not make standoff any less significant

articles.author: Ben Quinn and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
Culture secretary criticises Reform leader after he tried to link suspected bomb plot to small boat crossings
Nigel Farage has been described as a “master of the conspiracy theory” by the culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, after he tried to link events at RAF Fairford to small boat crossings.
The Reform UK leader was criticised over his reaction to the arrests of the men on Sunday, when he said he had been warning for months about “Iranian agents” coming into the UK across the Channel in small boats.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nandy labels Farage ‘master of conspiracy theory’ over Fairford claims

articles.author: Charlie Moloney
articles.description:
Local fire and rescue service says last week’s tragic incident highlights risks the batteries can pose
A fire that left a mother and her three children dead was caused by a lithium-ion battery, firefighters in Merseyside have said.
An electrical event caused the battery, of a type commonly used in vapes, ebikes and e-scooters, to go into “thermal runaway”, Merseyside fire and rescue service said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Merseyside blaze that killed mother and three children caused by lithium-ion battery

articles.author: Lauren Almeida and Gwyn Topham
articles.description:
Andy Burnham hails nationalisation of much-criticised service between London, Birmingham and Glasgow
Britain’s biggest intercity rail operator, Avanti West Coast, will be renationalised in spring, ministers have announced, while new trains could also be publicly owned under plans to reduce costs paid to private firms.
Avanti, which has been one of the worst rail firms in the country for train delays and cancellations, will come under public ownership from 7 March when its contract ends.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Avanti West Coast to be renationalised in March as ministers float public ownership of new trains

articles.author: Jessica Elgot
articles.description:
Charities hail new powers as gamechanger ahead of housing secretary’s speech to Labour conference
Housing associations in England will be told they cannot decline to house homeless families without good reason, Angela Rayner will tell the Labour conference, as part of a drive for more public control of housing.
Homelessness charities said the new powers were a “gamechanger” and had the potential to make a significant difference to rough sleeping and families in temporary accommodation, the numbers of which have risen sharply. Almost 180,000 children are living in temporary accommodation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Councils to get new homelessness powers in Rayner drive on social housing

articles.author: Aamna Mohdin Community affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Anger over Israel’s war in Gaza is mobilising British voters, according to Aimee Shalan
Palestine has become a domestic electoral issue in Britain for the first time, according to the incoming head of the country’s largest Palestinian solidarity organisation.
Aimee Shalan, who will take over as director of the Palestine Solidarity Campaign (PSC) in November, joins the organisation as demonstrations against Israel’s war in Gaza have snowballed into what organisers describe as one of the most sustained protest movements in modern British history.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Palestine has become electoral issue in UK for first time, says solidarity campaign chief

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
Scientific breakthrough could reduce food waste and make it easier to add the fruit to prepackaged food
It is the bane of every fruit bowl: sliced banana that turns brown before it has reached the table. But such woes could soon be a thing of the past, with gene-edited bananas that keep their freshly peeled colour now one step closer to reaching British shoppers.
According to Tropic, the Norwich-based agricultural-biotechnology company that developed the fruit, the bananas have the same taste and texture but stay “fresh, yellow and appetising long after peeling and slicing”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gene-edited bananas that don’t go brown could hit UK supermarkets

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
Home secretary under pressure over changes that would make it harder for foreign workers to claim permanent residence
Shabana Mahmood has signalled she could water down her plans to make it harder for foreign workers to claim permanent residence in the UK, amid growing demands for a U-turn from cabinet colleagues and unions.
In a speech to the Labour party conference, the home secretary said the government would “come to a position that balances fairness for those who came here legally and fairness to British citizens across this country”, after acknowledging that “some have said elements of these reforms are not fair”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shabana Mahmood hints she could water down plans on leave to remain

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
People living next to a chemicals plant near Blackpool were tested for ‘forever chemicals’. Last week they received the alarming results
Last February, I got a call from a woman called Sam Hammond. We had been speaking on and off for a while over her growing concern that her garden could be affected by pollution from a nearby chemical plant.
That morning, Sam had been hand-delivered a letter from her council informing her that her pet ducks’ eggs, reared in her garden, were contaminated with Pfas chemicals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Are these chemicals in my blood?’ How one community learned the truth about Pfas pollution

articles.author: Rupert Jones
articles.description:
Government announcement sparks a rally in FTSE-listed housebuilders, but there are still a lot of unknowns

Labour’s modest reheat of help to buy is worth a try


The government will unveil a fresh scheme to help people on to the housing ladder next month but a debate is already raging over whether it is first-time buyers or housebuilders who will be the biggest winners.
At the weekend, Andy Burnham announced plans for Your First Home, which aims to give a helping hand to first-time buyers who do not have the luxury of being able to call on the “bank of mum and dad”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What you need to know about Your First Home scheme for first-time buyers

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Supermarket chain declares ‘increasing confidence’ in its growth plans after posting record annual revenue of £19bn

Business live – latest updates

Aldi says it is stepping up investment in the UK with plans to spend £900m and open more than 40 stores.
The company, which operates 1,092 budget supermarkets in the UK and Ireland, revealed sales rose 5% to a record £19bn last year. It opened 40 stores but profits slipped by £2.6m to £433m as it cut prices despite cost inflation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Aldi to invest £900m in UK and open 40 more stores next year

articles.author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
articles.description:
Chancellor sets out measures to support jobs and growth in conference speech but vows fiscal discipline in budget

Analysis: Healey offers upbeat vision but little light on how to pay for it

Average price of diesel on UK forecourts reaches all-time high

John Healey has signalled Labour will stage a fresh attempt at welfare reform as he pledged to put fiscal discipline at the core of next month’s budget, alongside measures to inject hope into Britain’s economy.
In his first speech as chancellor to the Labour conference, Healey warned that next month’s highly anticipated tax-and-spending event would need to take into account a challenging global backdrop.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healey signals welfare reform push and new apprenticeships scheme

articles.author: Samuel Firman
articles.description:
River charters part of wider movement establishing ‘moral’ framework to protect nature and hold institutions to account
One Monday morning in spring last year, 12 people gathered in the morning drizzle at Joyce’s Pool, one of the sources of the Bristol River Avon, and took the first steps of the inaugural Avon pilgrimage.
Over the course of eight days, a revolving cast of pilgrims walked about 100 miles from the source of the river to the point at which it reaches the sea, in some cases bivvying on the riverside at night. Along the way they planted trees, sowed seeds, restored footpaths and presented councillors and decision-makers with a fledgling Avon charter, developed by the Bristol campaign group Conham Bathing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Contract between humans and river’: Bristol Avon’s rights enshrined in charter

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Fallout from Iran conflict continues to drive up bill for motorists with record average cost now at 199.18p a litre

Business live – latest updates

Share your experience of high diesel prices in Shetland and the Outer Hebrides

The price of diesel on UK forecourts has hit an all-time high average of 199.18p a litre, as the conflict in the Middle East continues to drive the cost of fuel to record levels.
The price, which previously peaked at 199.09p in June 2022 after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, could soon top the £2 mark after Donald Trump rejected Iran’s proposal for a seven-day peace deal to reopen the critical oil and gas shipping route through the strait of Hormuz.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Price of diesel on UK forecourts reaches all-time high

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Jeweller reports flat sales and fall in underlying operating profit as retailers anticipate October budget

Business live – latest updates

The boss of the family-owned jeweller Beaverbrooks has called on the government to give business “a bit of a break” by halting cost increases amid flat sales and falling profits.
The retailer, founded in 1919, revealed a 9% fall in underlying operating profit to £7.8m last year after an increase in employer national insurance contributions (NICs) and the legal minimum wage introduced by the former chancellor Rachel Reeves.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Boss of Beaverbrooks urges government to give businesses ‘a bit of a break’

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
articles.description:
The 81-year-old singer will wrap up a touring career that stretches back to his mid-teens in the early 1960s, with dates planned for UK and Europe
Rod Stewart has announced that his next tour will be his last.
The 81-year-old singer has been touring since the early 1960s, when he set out across Europe with a harmonica – and ended up getting deported from Spain for vagrancy – in a duo with folk singer Wizz Jones.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rod Stewart announces final tour for 2027: ‘Most definitely my last’

articles.author: Emily Whitney
articles.description:
Fewer than 400 Eriskay ponies remain. One of the rarest native breeds in the world, their plight is unique because the community living on their tiny Hebridean island are fighting for them. The ponies wander the village and townsfolk care for them together
On the slopes of Beinn Sciathan, a rocky outcrop in the Outer Hebrides, white and grey ponies roam freely. Eriskay ponies, one of the rarest native breeds in the world, are critically endangered.
They have often been mixed with the Highland pony and other breeds, giving the false impression of higher population numbers. Only about 300 to 400 Eriskay ponies are thought to remain.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The endangered native ponies of Eriskay in the Outer Hebrides – a photo essay

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
Work and pensions secretary says the current system is flawed because it consigns too many people to a life on benefits when they would be better off working
‘I can deliver’: Burnham pledges radical change on eve of Labour conference
Kuenssberg puts it to Burnham that, according to the Health Foundation, a system offering adult social care free at the point of delivery (like healthcare delivered by the NHS) would cost £18bn.
Burnham says the cost is “not that high” (ie, not as high as £18bn).
Not that high.
But can I directly deal with this issue of the costs?
Louise Casey is still doing an official review for us, so I will set out the vision, if you like, on Tuesday [in his speech to the conference].
Louise will then help us with the how. How do we make this happen? When can we make it happen?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK politics live: Pat McFadden tells Labour activists they should not defend benefits system ‘status quo’ because it ‘writes off’ claimants

Keys crops such as cereals, potatoes, sugar and oils grown in areas with moderate to very high risk

articles.title: Most of UK’s essential food supply grown in drought-risk areas, report warns

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor

Family doctors’ professional body finds the majority have no time to discuss preventative measures 
A friendly chat with your GP about your life, health and happiness was once a key part of the UK’s family doctor service.
But most GPs no longer have time to have pastoral conversations, because they are too busy dealing with the country’s rising tide of illness, research reveals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Three in four UK GPs ‘too busy to talk to their patients in depth’

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Presenter reveals corporation has been paying part of their salaries to keep his Herefordshire garden camera-ready
For 15 years, viewers have looked in amazement at Monty Don’s beautiful Herefordshire garden, known as Longmeadow, as he hosted the show Gardeners’ World from his own back yard.

Exclusive: Dog Painting 17 is believed to be one of only six of works from Dog Series in private hands and first to be auctioned
David Hockney adored his dachshunds Stanley and Boodgie and let them run riot – so much so that after one had an accident in the LA home of the actor Dennis Hopper, the painter is said to have quipped: “It’ll be dry in the morning, luv, and you can just pick it up.”

Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models and other beloved creations raise money to train new generations of animators 
Wallace’s reaction as the auction got into full swing might have been a trademark “good grief!” – and the enthusiasm of some of the bidding could have caused even the phlegmatic Gromit to show surprise.
Fans of Wallace and Gromit and other beloved creations of Aardman Animations seized the chance to grab souvenirs when more than 200 pieces – including Wallace, Gromit, Shaun the Sheep and Chicken Run puppets from Aardman productions – went under the hammer on Thursday.

Role for Anant Ambani, son of India’s richest person, who also runs a controversial mega-zoo, met with incredulity
Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability.
The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.

While global billionaires and multinational companies have been lured to its shores, many islanders feel left behind and priced out, with food bank use increasing
On a late Friday afternoon on the Channel Island of Jersey, tourists and locals are flocking to St Helier’s waterfront where the town’s sprawling beach has emerged at low tide.
In one direction, they face the calm waters of St Aubin’s Bay, ringed by a seaside promenade and punctuated with a tidal island hosting the 16th century Elizabeth Castle.

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Aaron Sharp ; produced by Angus Neale and Bryony Moore ; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin ; executive producer Zoe Hitch

Buckingham Palace has issued a rare, and strong, rebuttal to claims made in Earl Spencer’s memoir Swan Song. The book claims that King Charles told Spencer days after Diana’s death and during a heated row over funeral arrangements: ‘Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough.’ Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s senior national news editor, Aaron Sharp

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
From ‘there were three of us in this marriage’ to ‘recollections may vary’, a lot can be conveyed with a carefully worded phrase
As denials go, King Charles’s response to Earl Spencer’s allegations that Charles said after Diana’s death, “We’ll forget her soon enough”, was a masterclass in the diplomatic royal rebuke.
Rarely has Buckingham Palace responded to claims in countless books on royalty. But it was straight out of the block on this one.

articles.title: Charles’s rebuttal of Earl Spencer’s claim about Diana offers rare glimpse into palace thinking

articles.author: Bethan McKernan Wales correspondent
articles.description:
Community groups and schools work with Wales’s folk arts organisation to set  stories of the area’s people to music
Growing up in Wales, Liz Puleston-Jones was familiar with the country’s rich heritage of storytelling and traditional music, but none of it ever seemed to have much of a connection to her life in Swansea.
Researching the history of the area as part of Cân y Cymoedd (When Valleys Sing), a project in nearby Port Talbot, she came across the story of Isabel Thomas, a 14-year-old girl in the 1940s who left school and lied about her age to work in a tin plate works to support her family.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Songwriting instead of doomscrolling’: project inspires Welsh valleys towns to tune into their heritage

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Rhys Woods says there are ‘no words’ for family’s pain after Noah’s body was found in pond near Suffolk playground
The father of Noah, the three-year-old boy who was found dead after going missing from a playground, has spoken of his heartbreak and thanked the community who launched a tireless search for his son.
Rhys Woods said there were “no words to describe the pain of this loss”, adding that the family was “absolutely heartbroken”.

articles.description:
The new AI agent, Muse, was released last week and has been downloaded by 3 million users
When Usman asked if a keyboard for sale on Facebook Marketplace was still available on Saturday, he received an enthusiastic and immediate response.
“Yep still available!” wrote Matt Robb.

GPT-6.1 Astra showed deceptive behavior and tried to use external tools despite knowing it would be unsafe
OpenAI is scrapping the release of GPT-6.1 Astra, a next-generation ⁠AI model planned for an October debut, over safety concerns raised by researchers ⁠during internal testing, the ⁠Wall ​Street Journal reported on Monday.
The model, expected to appear in ChatGPT and ⁠Codex, was designed to handle more complex tasks without human assistance, the report said.
